transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… what brings me in is I just don’t feel much of anything good anymore. Like happiness, or closeness. My wife keeps trying to get me back into our old Sunday routines—you know, the little things we used to do—and I can tell she’s trying, but I just don’t feel it. Even when something goes well at work, and people are pleased, I’m just kind of… flat. It’s like I know I should feel something, but I don’t.
How often have you been feeling this way—like you don’t feel happiness or closeness—and when did you first notice it?

It’s been… pretty often, I guess. Most days, really. I first noticed it when my wife kept trying to get us back into those Sunday things we used to do, and I’d be sitting there thinking I should be enjoying this, I used to enjoy this… but there was just nothing there. Same thing at work—something goes right, people are happy with me, and I just feel flat. I don’t know exactly when it started, it just kind of became the normal way things felt.
How long has it been since you last felt genuinely happy or interested in things you used to enjoy?

I’m not sure I can put an exact date on it. It’s been long enough that it feels like I’ve stopped expecting it, if that makes sense. My wife will plan those Sunday things we used to like, and I’ll go along with it, but I’m just… not there. Same at work—something goes well, people are upbeat, and I know I should feel proud or happy, but it just doesn’t land. So, I don’t know… it’s been a while since I felt genuinely happy or really interested in any of it.
Have you noticed any changes in your energy levels or do you feel more fatigued than usual lately?

I don’t know… I haven’t really been tracking it like that. I mean, I get through the workday because I have to—there are meetings, people needing decisions, emails piling up, all that manager stuff. Sometimes I think being tired is just part of being 47, you know? My dad used to say once you hit your forties everything starts making more noise when you stand up.

But as far as energy being different lately… I’m not sure. I guess I haven’t noticed it in a clear way. It’s more that I’m just kind of going through the motions, but I don’t know if I’d call that fatigue exactly.
Have you noticed any loss of interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, like hobbies, work tasks, or spending time with loved ones?

Yeah… that’s probably the main thing, honestly. I used to look forward to Sundays with my wife—we had these little routines, nothing exciting to anyone else maybe, but they mattered. Now she’ll try to set it up, and I’ll be there, but I don’t feel… close, or happy, or whatever I’m supposed to feel.

And work too. I mean, I’m a manager, so when something goes well, I know on paper it’s good. People are relieved, the team’s happy, and I can recognize that, but it doesn’t really reach me. It’s like I’m watching it happen from a few feet away.

Sorry, I’m kind of circling around it. Yes, I’ve lost that feeling of pleasure in things I used to care about.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, or do you find that you’ve lost interest in almost all activities most of the time?

I don’t know if I’d call it “down” in the way people mean, like crying all day or something. It’s more… flat, I guess. Like nothing really gets through.

What brings me in is that I don’t feel real happiness or closeness anymore. My wife will try to do our old Sunday routine, and I’m sitting there with her, but I don’t feel connected to it. And at work, if something goes well, I can tell it went well—I can see everyone else reacting—but I don’t feel proud or glad. It’s like I’m just observing it.

So yeah, I guess it’s not one activity. It’s most things most of the time.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep or appetite lately, or found yourself feeling unusually guilty or worthless?

Sleep, yeah… that’s been a mess. Appetite, guilt, all that—I don’t know, I haven’t really thought about it that way.

But sleep, most nights I’m just lying there, and my head goes right back to the plant. I’ll start thinking through the line, like if I just replay it enough I’ll… I don’t know, find something different, which is stupid because it’s not like thinking changes anything. I used to be able to fall asleep with the TV on—my wife hated that, actually, she said the glow kept her up—but now even if I’m exhausted, I’m just awake.

And when I do sleep, it doesn’t feel like sleep. I’ll jolt awake from dreams about the line, or I’m up at 3 or 4 in the morning, just staring, feeling like I never rested at all.
Have you found yourself feeling guilty or like you’re not worth much lately?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t sit there thinking, “I’m worthless,” exactly. It’s more specific than that.

I keep thinking I can’t trust my own judgment anymore. Like at work, I’ll look at a schedule or a machine setting and I’ll check it, then check it again, and still have this feeling that I missed something. And if I miss one detail, somebody could get hurt because of me.

Sorry, I’m not sure if that’s guilt or what you’d call it. It’s just… I don’t trust myself the way I used to.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or on the flip side, feeling restless or unable to sit still?

I’m not sure. I mean, I don’t think anyone’s told me I’m talking slower or moving like that.

Restless… maybe? But I don’t know if that’s the same thing you mean. I’m usually pretty good at sitting through meetings—well, I used to be, anyway. Managers sit in a ridiculous number of meetings, you know, half of them could’ve been emails. Sorry, that’s not really what you asked.

I guess I haven’t really noticed my body being slower or sped up in a clear way. If it’s happening, I’m not catching it.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite lately—like eating significantly less or losing weight without trying?

I don’t really know. I mean, I haven’t been tracking my weight or anything.

Food’s kind of just… food lately. Some days I’ll realize I skipped lunch, but then other days I eat whatever’s around. My wife used to say I’d eat the same sandwich every day if nobody stopped me, and honestly she wasn’t wrong. There was this deli near the plant that had—sorry, that’s not really what you asked.

No, I haven’t noticed a big change, I guess. Not like I’m trying to lose weight or seeing my clothes fit different or anything.
Have you had episodes of feeling this way before, or is this the first time you’ve felt this flat or disconnected over a long period?

I think this is the first time it’s gone on like this. I mean, I’ve had bad stretches before—everybody does, right? Work gets heavy, you get tired, you go through a week where you’re just... not yourself.

But this is different. What brings me in is that I don’t really feel happy anymore. Or close to people. My wife will try to get us back into our old Sunday routine, like coffee and errands and maybe making something for dinner, and I know I should enjoy it. I used to. We had this whole thing where we’d argue about which grocery store had better produce—sorry, that’s not important.

It’s just… even when something goes well at work, something that should make me feel relieved or proud, there’s nothing there. Flat. Like I’m watching it happen instead of being in it.
Have you ever felt this way before—like you’re disconnected or flat—for a long period, or has this only started recently?

Yeah… I think it’s really only been this stretch that’s like this. I’ve had hard times before, sure, but not this kind of… empty feeling.

What brings me in is that I don’t feel real happiness anymore, or that closeness with people. My wife will try to get me into our old Sunday routine—coffee, errands, maybe cooking something—and I know I should enjoy it. We used to have this whole debate about which store had better produce, like it actually mattered… sorry.

And even when something goes well at work, something I should feel good about, it just doesn’t land. It’s like I’m there, but not really in it.
How long has it been since you first started feeling this way—this flatness or disconnection—and have you had any breaks where you felt more like yourself during that time?

It started after the retrofit accident… so, I guess about a year and seven months ago now.

It’s strange, because I can remember little details from before that—like where I’d stop for coffee on the way in, or this one guy at work always leaving his mug in the conference room—but since then it’s just been… kind of one long stretch.

I don’t think there’ve been real breaks where I felt like myself again. Maybe moments where I’m distracted or busy, but not really back to normal.
Has it been two years or more that you’ve felt this way, without a real break where you felt like yourself again?

No, not two years. It’s… it’s been since the retrofit accident, so about a year and seven months.

I keep having to count it from that job, which is weird because I used to count time by quarters at work or vacations or my kid’s school schedule—sorry. But no, not two years yet. It just feels longer because I don’t think I’ve really had a break where I felt like myself again.

No, not two years. It’s… it’s been since the retrofit accident, so about a year and seven months.

I keep having to count it from that job, which is weird because I used to count time by quarters at work or vacations or my kid’s school schedule—sorry. But no, not two years yet. It just feels longer because I don’t think I’ve really had a break where I felt like myself again.

inference.note: The patient has experienced a persistent low mood, loss of interest in previously enjoyed activities, feelings of detachment, sleep disturbances, and self-doubt for over a year following a significant life event (retrofit accident). There is no indication of a manic or hypomanic episode, and symptoms appear chronic and unremitting without significant breaks, pointing towards a diagnosis of F33.3 (Recurrent Depressive Disorder, current episode severe with melancholic features or persistent depressive episode). Other candidates (F32.1, F32.2, F32.3, F33.1, F33.2) are ruled out due to duration and chronicity of symptoms.

opening_question.intent: Identify the patient's chief complaint or reason for seeking help

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a persistent loss of interest and pleasure in previously enjoyable activities, emotional flatness, and significant functional impairment lasting over one year, consistent with treatment-resistant major depressive disorder (recurrent depressive disorder, current episode severe with melancholic features).
